LESSON: KENYAN FOLK SONGS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Critical Appreciation
Topic 3.1: Kenyan Folk Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan Folk Songs, part of Critical Appreciation in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: What is a folk song? 2. What is the essence of analysing folk songs? 3. How can folksongs be used to address issues in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. examine different performance media of Kenyan folk songs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Folk Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the styles in selected Kenyan folk songs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Folk Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. evaluate how the elements of music feature in the performance of a Kenyan folksong,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Folk Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. analyse the role of expressive devices in Kenyan folksongs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Folk Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. analyse the message communicated in a folk song,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Folk Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. value the essence of performance of Kenyan folksongs in society.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Folk Songs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to or watch live or recorded Kenyan traditional folk music with controlled volume and classify performance media. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light (Apply this adaptation in the subsequent learning experiences involving watching),
2. in pairs or purposive groups, discuss the role 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan Folk Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner listens critically to folksongs and speaks/mime clearly as they discuss

messages in folksongs.

• Citizenship: The learner listens to folksongs from different Kenyan cultures developing respect and acceptance of

heterogeneity.

• Learning to learn: The learner uses research skills to examine the elements of music.

• Digital literacy: The learner uses digital devices to search for music on the internet.

Values:
• Integrity: The learner uses the internet appropriately when sourcing for folksongs of Kenya.

• Patriotism: The learner is made aware of his or her own culture through exposure to folksongs from Kenya.

• Unity: The learner collaborates with others as they discuss the role of performance media in folksongs.

• Respect: The learner appreciates others’ views as they give personal responses while listening to folksongs.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Pollution: The learner gets sensitised on noise pollution by controlling the volume while listening to folk music.

• Life skills: The learner is inspired by watching Kenyan folksongs artistes to identify and nurture own talent.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. examine different performance media of Kenyan folk songs,
2. analyse the styles in selected Kenyan folk songs,
3. evaluate how the elements of music feature in the performance of a Kenyan folksong,
4. analyse the role of expressive devices in Kenyan folksongs,
5. analyse the message communicated in a folk song,
6. value the essence of performance of Kenyan folksongs in society.
